title: Fix the rule defects of execute

release_levels.reason: The rules of execute now agree, and one stop changes: an all-blocking gap ends at the final report.
The manual stops listing the all-blocking gap as a stop.

units.title: Make the rules of execute agree
Honor a caller's preference in doctor and handoff

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc belongs to the docs unit

decisions.decision: Defect 1: which units does a review row cover?
decisions.ruling: An earlier unit of any kind. references/review-unit.md changes to agree with the refusal in workflows/folder.md and interview item 10a.

decisions.decision: Defect 2: which folders does each recall read?
decisions.ruling: Both the per-unit recall and the plan-level recall read docs/memory/decisions/, docs/memory/problems/ and docs/memory/gaps/.
decisions.rejected: Three per unit and two at setup; decisions and gaps only.

decisions.decision: Defect 3: which raw git commands may the run use?
decisions.ruling: Any read-only git command. Of the commands that write, only the ones that references/rules.md names: the index row commits, the staging discipline, git merge and its --abort in references/setup.md, and git worktree remove in workflows/all.md. The git submodule and git clone lines in workflows/folder.md are text that the run reports to a person, so they are not exceptions.
decisions.rejected: Remove the raw commands from the run; also list the commands that the run only reports.

decisions.decision: Defect 4: does the never rule on gates name gates.keeps?
decisions.ruling: Yes. references/rules.md names gates.unit, gates.wave, gates.plan and gates.keeps.

decisions.decision: Defect 5: what does the delete refusal cover?
decisions.ruling: Refuse a deletion outside the unit's Owns, except a file that the run created. The approved Owns list is the consent to delete.
decisions.rejected: Owns only when the unit file names the deletion; keep the rule and exempt edit units.

decisions.decision: Defect 6: how do the prompts of doctor and handoff go away in a run?
decisions.ruling: execute declares a caller preference in the skill's arguments, as text that starts with prefer: and that the skill never reads as a name. To doctor: prefer: report only, which offers no fix and asks nothing. To handoff: prefer: the one thread is this plan's run. Both skills get a short section that honors the prefix, as git-workflow honors a declared preference. An argument with only the prefix counts as empty, so doctor checks every project and handoff writes next. Names, when a caller has them, come before the prefix.
decisions.rejected: Only execute's files change; change the defaults of the two skills; the prose beside the skill call; a dedicated flag per skill.

decisions.decision: Defects 7 and 8: SKILL.md pauses on an all-blocking gap (H6) and on an agent that errors twice (H4), but references/blocking.md goes to the final report and continues. Which wins?
decisions.ruling: H6 goes: an all-blocking gap ends at the final report, as references/blocking.md says. H4 stays a pause, as references/pause.md says, so references/blocking.md stops treating a dead agent as an isolated block. Do not renumber the other H ids.
decisions.rejected: blocking.md wins for both, which needed a new failure path for each agent type and did not converge in three review rounds; SKILL.md wins for both.

decisions.decision: Does the change need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: No. Every owned file is prose, so the plan lands no runnable code and the wave review is the check.
decisions.rejected: A review unit that runs the security half.

decisions.decision: Does a ledger review run over these edits?
decisions.ruling: No. These edits change rules on purpose, and a ledger proves that a rewrite keeps every rule. The wave review judges each edit against its unit file.
decisions.rejected: Run the ledger and mark each changed rule as a drop.

decisions.decision: How far does the cascade behind a review row reach, now that rows cover units of any kind and a dead reviewer marks a row failed?
decisions.ruling: A failed, unresolved or skipped review row skips each later review row and each later unit of any kind that a later row covers.
decisions.rejected: Failed too but code units only; skipped rows only.

decisions.decision: An agent errors twice in a parallel edit wave, and H4 pauses the run. What happens first?
decisions.ruling: Wait for the other reports, run the gates, and commit each green unit. Leave the dead unit's edits uncommitted, and name them in the gaps entry and the pause report. The folder then reads RUNNING — paused at unit <n>: agent died.
decisions.rejected: Keep the current words and accept an open gap; pause at once.

gaps.text: waves.md "On failure" said "never mid-wave" and SKILL.md H4 said "Commit what is safe", both outside the Edits, though H4 pauses · assumed the step 5 exception and pause.md govern; closed: wave review round 1 raised both, U1 fixed them in round 2, reviewer clean
